newsitem.title: CHINA: World Bank may lend $150 mln to west China region.
newsitem.headline: World Bank may lend $150 mln to west China region.

text.p: The World Bank is considering lending China $150 million to end poverty and boost environmental protection in the westernmost Xinjiang region, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The loan would be part of the 2.3 billion ($277 million) second phase of a project in Xinjiang's poverty-stricken Tarim basin in the south of the region, it said. It would be one of the World Bank's biggest agricultural projects in China.

The loan for the second phase that mostly involves irrigation and improvement of rural infrastructure, would be a hard loan with annual interest at more than 6.0 percent and a repayment term of 15 years, the newspaper said.
The World Bank is cutting the size of soft loans to China, it said.

The bank gave $125 million in loans to help the first phase of the project to help 2.3 million people living in poverty. The first four-year phase, with total investment of 1.65 billion ($200 million), was completed last year, the newspaper said.
The bank has already extended $25.2 billion in soft and hard loans to Chinese projects, with just $1.84 billion in hard loans for agricultural projects, it added.
Of the bank's total loans, $6.6 billion has been used in 47 agriculture projects, accounting for about 26 percent of the total.
